name: work-humanizer
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and any agent that loads SKILL.md
short: Rewrites AI-sounding work writing so it reads like a careful person wrote it, and keeps every fact and commitment.
what: work-humanizer edits sales copy, support replies, HR and legal letters, emails, docs and landing pages. It lists every fact and how certain it is, rewrites the piece in a plain voice, then checks the result sentence by sentence against that list. When a draft is thin, interview mode asks you up to five questions and builds the piece from your answers. It can also write from your own notes or a voice memo transcript.
who: People who use AI to draft work writing where the exact wording matters. The README says it doesn't get text past AI detectors, so it won't help if that's your goal.
needs: A coding agent that loads skills
Python, only if you want to run the optional `check.py` sweep yourself

steps.title: Or copy the folder
steps.text: Copy `skills/work-humanizer` into `~/.claude/skills/work-humanizer` for Claude Code, `~/.codex/skills/work-humanizer` for Codex, or your agent's skills folder.

steps.title: Run the mechanical check (optional)
steps.text: It looks for dashes, semicolons, stock AI words, filler transitions and sentence length.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Use work-humanizer on this and interview me first: <paste draft>

watch: The test results in the README come from small samples judged by AI models, and the authors designed the test themselves. The README asks you to read the evidence folder before quoting any number.
Interview mode was tested with an AI answering for the writer, not real people.
